name: Mauritius
summary_text: Mauritius is workable for trans visitors — the Indian Ocean's most liveable jurisdiction. The Supreme Court repealed Section 250 in 2023, decriminalising same-sex conduct; the Equal Opportunities Act covers discrimination; and in 2024 Jeanny Michelle Karla Fanfan competed as the first trans woman in Miss Universe Mauritius — a public milestone met with national discussion rather than violence. There is no legal gender recognition law (a barrier highlighted by AfricLaw), and social conservatism persists, but tourist infrastructure is extensive and accustomed to diverse visitors, and there is no documented police targeting pattern. For a visitor: no legal exposure, functioning courts, low street risk in tourist areas.

sources.title: Mauritius | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): the Supreme Court repealed Section 250 in 2023, decriminalising same-sex conduct - advances for LGB people, less evident for trans/intersex people. No same-sex marriage; the Equal Opportunities Act 2008 and Workers' Rights Act 2019 protect against sexual-orientation discrimination; intersex children can be registered as 'undetermined' (2021 Civil Status Act) but nonconsensual procedures not banned; Pride since 2005 with counter-protests; some anti-LGBTIQ hate speech during 2024 elections.

sources.title: Miss Universe Mauritius 2024: A landmark in the legal battle for transgender equality | AfricLaw
sources.claim_summary: AfricLaw (Aug 2024) by Lakshmi Kanhiya: Miss Universe Mauritius 2024 - the historic participation of Jeanny Michelle Karla Fanfan as the first trans woman contestant marks a milestone; the article discusses the broader legal and social challenges for trans people in Mauritius (Civil Status Act 1981, Central Population Database, stigmatisation, lack of legal recognition).

sources.title: Mauritius - United States Department of State
sources.claim_summary: US State Department 2016 Human Rights Report for Mauritius: official assessment - sodomy law (Section 250) rarely enforced; societal discrimination exists; no legal gender recognition.

Young Queer Alliance policy brief (July 2021): 'Administrative recognition of Trans People in Mauritius' - argues for legal gender recognition; notes the WHO's ICD-11 removed trans categories from mental disorders (2019) and calls on Mauritius to join countries recognising gender identity in law.

sources.title: Over 80 Nations Support Statement at Human Rights Council on LGBT Rights - U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Geneva
sources.claim_summary: US Mission in Geneva (March 2011): post on LGBT rights in the UN context - US diplomatic advocacy for SOGI rights at the Human Rights Council, relevant to Mauritius's international human-rights environment.
